title: [Chapitre] VIII. Analysis situs (quatrième mouture) : notes manuscrites (26/06-04/07/1986).

deep.reconstruction:
Setting, carried over from p.67: M is a set of 'pieces' (strata or cells of a tame space). It carries a symmetric antireflexive relation ∥. On p.67 this is X ∥ Y ⇔ X̄ ∩ Ȳ = ∅. A 'support' is a subset of M that is closed under the polarity of ∥: write cosupp°(A) = {y | y ∥ x for all x ∈ A} and supp° = cosupp°∘cosupp°. The supports form Σ_M, ordered by inclusion. Σ_M is a complete lattice: infima are intersections, and Sup S_i = supp°(∪ S_i). The map S ↦ ∁S = cosupp°(S) is an order-reversing involution. In modern terms this is the complete ortholattice of orthoclosed subsets of an orthogonality space.

On this page L ⊂ M is the subset of 'points' or minimal pieces. Each x ∈ M has a 'shadow' omb°(x) ⊂ L, with omb°(x) = {x} for x ∈ L. The relation on M is assumed to be pulled back from L: X ∥ Y ⇔ every point of omb°X is ∥ to every point of omb°Y. Grothendieck tentatively links this to a hypothesis 'Mag L 2', a dimensional genericity condition.

Grothendieck wants to compare Σ_M with Σ_L.
- He first asks whether S ↦ S ∩ L sends supports to supports.
- Because ∥ is pulled back, cosupp°_M(A) = cosupp°_M(omb°A), where omb°(A) = ∪_{x∈A} omb°(x).
- In the margin he notes the consequence supp°X = supp°(omb°X).
- Intersecting with L gives cosupp°_M(A) ∩ L = cosupp°_L(omb°A). Since every support has the form cosupp°_M(A), S ∩ L is a support of L.
- In the other direction he proposes Σ_L → Σ_M, A ↦ supp°_M(A), and asks (with a '?') whether this equals {x ∈ M | omb°x ⊂ A}.
- He proves one inclusion: if omb°x ⊂ A, then supp°x = supp°(omb°x) ⊂ supp°_M(A), so x ∈ supp°_M(A).
- The page ends with 'Mais inversement, supposons…'. The converse is finished on p.69, which concludes that the two maps are mutually inverse isomorphisms of ortholattices. He calls this formal for any M → P(L) restricting to x ↦ {x} on L.

Check of the formal fact. For A ⊂ M, cosupp°_M(A) = {y | omb°y ⊂ cosupp°_L(omb°A)}. Hence the supports of M are exactly the sets {y | omb°y ⊂ C} with C a support of L. Their trace on L is C, because omb° of a point is that point. The double polar of A ∈ Σ_L computed in M equals {x | omb°x ⊂ A}. The purpose is to reduce the lattice of supports of a stratified or tame space to one computed on its points or vertices; p.69 notes that this lattice is P(L) when ∥ is ≠.
errors: No mathematical error. The equality on this page is left with a '?' and only one inclusion is proved here; it is completed on the next page.

The genericity hypothesis ('Mag L 2') is actually unnecessary once ∥_M is defined as the pullback of ∥_L via omb° with omb°(x) = {x} on L. It is only needed to justify that the closure-disjointness relation on M is of this pulled-back form.
On the page 'supp°(x) ∈ supp°_M(A)' should read ⊂.

ideas.what: Supports as polar-closed subsets for a symmetric antireflexive relation, forming a complete lattice with an orthocomplement (already set up on p.67)
ideas.modern_name: Orthogonality space / complete ortholattice of orthoclosed sets (Galois polarity)

ideas.what: Transfer of the support lattice along a 'shadow' map M → P(L) that restricts to x ↦ {x} on L: S ↦ S∩L and A ↦ {x | omb x ⊂ A} are inverse ortholattice isomorphisms
ideas.modern_name: Invariance of the orthoclosure lattice under pullback of an orthogonality relation (dense/generating subset)

deep.surprise_reason: A routine Galois-connection computation inside Grothendieck's unpublished tame-topology ('analysis situs') drafts. It is correct but standard lattice theory; the only mildly notable point is the use of orthogonality-space structure for supports in a stratified setting.
transcription_corrections: 'supp°(x) ∈ supp°_M(A)' on the next-to-last line should be read as 'supp°(x) ⊂ supp°_M(A)'.
The last formula 'cosupp°_L(omb(A))' should be read 'cosupp°_L(omb°(A))'.
'Mag L 2' is likely a reference to a numbered hypothesis or condition (possibly a label), with 'une généricité dimensionnelle' added above; the struck-through text is illegible.
